Recommended read. We are just starting to understand how AI shapes decisions and judgment. At first glance, this might look like a simple, niche passion research project. However, it's an important research direction for understanding where AI's true value emerges and how to optimize agent-human collaboration. If we can better understand when to defer to AI and when expert/human judgment matters, I think this unlocks tremendous value. Yes, it matters for organizations adopting AI, but I see it as an interesting way to better measure human-agent collaboration and discover new, optimal ways to augment collective intelligence. New Anthropic research: How AI agents shape experts' judgment calls When experts delegate work to an agent, do they still make the key decisions? We tested this in a randomized trial with 50 professional data analysts.
